$comment: Water as a surface grid (docs/WATER_SURFACE_GRID.md, ADR 0060): a depth per 1 m column moving to its neighbours by the local-inertial law, in sleeping water chunks of 16 x 16 columns. Rates are real and counted in game time (the day/night clock's: a 20-minute day is 72x real time) x the world's water speed (`speed`, the default of the server's `water_speed`). tickEvery: server ticks per water tick. theta: the face law's weighting (1 the plain scheme, below 1 damped; de Almeida et al. 2012). cfl: a substep's share of the time a wave takes to cross a column. maxSubsteps: the most substeps a water tick takes (more, and the water runs slow that tick). sleepBandM, sleepSwingM: a chunk sleeps once no level in it drifted more than sleepBandM over calmS water s (the means of the window's two halves within half of it; tight: a chunk asleep off its level gives it back as a wave) and none swung more than sleepSwingM in it (a deep reservoir's slosh, a running river's jitter of a centimetre or two, steady on the whole, is calm; BUGS.md #41). wakeBandM: how far a sleeping chunk's account (what its awake neighbours sent it) may move its water before it wakes. releaseS: a woken chunk takes what it owes over this long, by depth. jumpM2s: a shared face's change in a substep (m2/s) that wakes a sleeping chunk at once. releaseM: a free column this far off its rest frees the held water beside it, so a change spreads as far as it reaches. restCut, restBack: a free column whose rest inflow (the flow the water as generated brings it, by face) comes less than restCut from columns still in the rest leaves the rest, its springs and sinks with it, and one whose comes more than restBack from them returns: so the reach below a dam, down the river it carried to a junction whose other river brings most of the flow or the lake it ran into, keeps no spring to refill it and dries (BUGS.md #41). keptSteady: a chunk falls asleep with its flows kept (a river running through it, a reservoir spilling over its dam: what it is taken to pass on asleep), each edge face carrying its mean over the calm window if the means of the window's two halves agree within this share of the larger, none if not (a slosh to and fro has no flow to keep) (BUGS.md #41). stillDampS, stillDampMs: water slower than stillDampMs (m/s) loses its flow over stillDampS (s) besides its friction (a drag that stops at stillDampMs, so faster water feels a constant stillDampMs / stillDampS of it): deep still water's slosh, which Manning's friction barely touches (a 3.5 m deep basin sloshed +-1 cm for half an hour), settles in minutes, and a dammed reservoir falls asleep (BUGS.md #41). editReach: an edit frees the water within this many columns. fillHysteresis: how far past half a drawn step (in the liquid's fill steps) a level must move before its cells are written again. currentStillMs: water slower than this (m/s) has no current (docs/WATER_SURFACE_GRID.md §2c). currentDepthM: water shallower than this (m) has no current, a wet film's flow over its depth being noise. riverCurrentMaxMs: the fastest an untouched river's current runs (m/s; its speed is Manning's on the map river's fall at the column's depth, or the river's flow over that depth where faster (a level reach runs too), and a steep chute's would be a torrent; 1.5 leaves a swimmer at the swim layer's 3 m/s headway upstream). riverFallReachM: how far up and down its course (m) an untouched river's fall is averaged for its current, which runs on the larger of that mean and its own segment's fall: the map's courses never rise, so where the land dips a course is held level for a hundred metres or more and drops after it, and on its own fall such a reach ran at its flow over its depth alone, a tenth of the reach above it (BUGS.md #42). stepBudget: the most column-substeps a water tick may take (its substeps times its awake columns, at least one substep): water runs on game time, a tick of it is seconds of water, and many awake chunks could take the server longer than a tick; past the budget the rest of the tick's water time is lost (the water runs slow, not the game). Only where the water runs on the server's own thread (inline: tests, a fallback); on its own thread (ADR 0062, docs/WATER_SURFACE_GRID.md §2d) the water instead owes the time it hasn't run and runs it as fast as it can, at most threadStepBudget column-substeps a run (so it still answers edits and save requests between runs), and past maxOwedS of owed water time (water s, game time x speed: 360 is 5 real s at the 72x day) the rest is dropped and its clock slows. liquids: each liquid the grid moves (the first is the one it draws): its block, Manning's roughness (s/m^(1/3)), its weir coefficient (m^0.5/s; the generator sizes chute streams by it) and its running block (the generator's chute streams). Run `node shared/fluids/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-world/src/flow.gen.rs is stale.
